title: Every uploaded version carries build-provenance readable at runtime
iWant: one HTTP request to the running Worker to name the commit, the build time, and the CI run URL
soThat: the served surface is self-identifying without any dashboard step

acceptanceCriteria.description: The `build-and-upload` workflow injects the commit sha, the build ISO 8601 timestamp, and the CI run URL into the Worker's bundle (as build-time constants, as `vars`, or via the Deploy Adapter's `describeVersion` surface); the values are readable from within the Worker at request time.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a `build-and-upload` run at commit C at time T triggered from CI run R
acceptanceCriteria.when: the resulting Worker's runtime code reads the provenance surface
acceptanceCriteria.then: the surface returns an object whose `versionSha` equals C's short sha, whose `builtAt` equals T formatted as ISO 8601, and whose `ciRunUrl` equals R

acceptanceCriteria.description: A fixed health-probe path (project-declared, `/healthz` by common default) responds with a JSON body carrying stable field names `versionSha`, `builtAt`, and `ciRunUrl` on any deployed URL (preview alias, version id, production).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a deployed Worker at any of the three URL kinds
acceptanceCriteria.when: an HTTP GET hits the project's declared health-probe path
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response body is JSON with fields `versionSha`, `builtAt`, `ciRunUrl`; all three fields are populated with non-empty strings; the response status is in the success set

acceptanceCriteria.description: The Served-surface Verifier uses the `versionSha` field on the probe response body (the git commit sha the served version was built from) to confirm the promoted version is the version being served; the value the verifier compares against is the promote record's `versionSha` field, distinct from the promote record's `promotedVersionId` (the vendor-assigned version UUID). A promote whose post-promote probe returns a `versionSha` that does not match the promote record's `versionSha` fails the release.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a promote of version W with promote record `{ promotedVersionId: 'v-uuid-W', versionSha: 'sha-W' }`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the verifier's post-promote probe returns a body whose `versionSha` reads `sha-P` (a stale prior version)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the verifier records the mismatch as `PROMOTE_VERIFY_FAILED` with the observed `sha-P` and the expected `sha-W`; the release is not marked successful
